ClinicalDocument.title: SYNTHETIC RECORD, NOT A REAL MEDICAL RECORD — Progress Note 2 — Focused Visit (Follow-up) — Booker T. Washington

code.originalText: One-week blood pressure and kidney safety check with nephrology consultation

text.paragraph: One-week blood pressure and kidney safety check. [S]

Mr. Washington returns one week after starting amlodipine and losartan for severe hypertension with stage G3b chronic kidney disease. His home readings, taken twice daily, have fallen from above 200 systolic to the 160s and 170s over 100s. He has had one mild frontal headache this week, fewer than before, and no chest pain, breathlessness, weakness, confusion, or sudden change in vision. His palpitations are less frequent. He has had no lightheadedness on standing and no ankle swelling, and he takes both medicines every morning. His reading vision is still blurred and he still gets up twice a night to urinate. He asks how to keep to the plan on travel days. His nephrology consultation, kidney ultrasound, and echocardiogram were done today. [S]

list.item:
Severe hypertension with hypertensive kidney disease, improving (I12.9). Blood pressure 172/104 mmHg, down from 212/128 a week ago, with no symptoms of acute target-organ damage, but still far above target. The echocardiogram today shows concentric left ventricular hypertrophy with an ejection fraction of 60 percent. [S]
Increase losartan to 100 mg daily.
Continue amlodipine 10 mg daily.
Home readings twice daily; emergency department warning signs reviewed again.
Travel plan: medicines in his carry-on bag, a home cuff on trips, and low-sodium choices when eating out.

Chronic kidney disease stage G3b A3 (N18.32). One week after starting losartan, creatinine is 2.2 mg/dL (up 5 percent from 2.1), eGFR 34, and potassium 4.6 mmol/L. Urine albumin-creatinine ratio 820 mg/g at diagnosis, so his risk category is very high. Both kidneys are small (9.4 and 9.6 cm) and echogenic without hydronephrosis, which fits long-standing hypertensive nephrosclerosis. Nephrology agrees with the plan. [S]
Start dapagliflozin 10 mg daily: eGFR is above 20 and albuminuria above 200 mg/g.
Accept a creatinine rise of up to 30 percent with losartan and dapagliflozin.
Potassium and creatinine at the three-week check.
Avoid NSAIDs; sick-day rule: hold dapagliflozin and losartan on any day with vomiting, diarrhea, or poor fluid intake, and call.
Pneumococcal conjugate vaccine and hepatitis B vaccine dose 1 today.

Hypertensive retinopathy, both eyes (H35.033). Arteriolar narrowing and arteriovenous nicking without hemorrhages, exudates, or papilledema on last week's dilated examination; reading blur unchanged. [S]
Dilated eye examination yearly.
Report any sudden change in vision at once.

Mild anemia of chronic kidney disease (D63.1). Hemoglobin 12.6 g/dL with ferritin 210 ng/mL and transferrin saturation 26 percent: iron replete. [S]
Hemoglobin at least yearly while in stage G3.

Hyperlipidemia (E78.5). Atorvastatin 20 mg started a week ago for LDL cholesterol 138 mg/dL, as recommended for adults 50 and older with eGFR below 60; no muscle symptoms. [S]
Continue atorvastatin; no routine repeat LDL, per KDIGO.
